answer: Because software clones easily pass tests like writing a sonnet or naming a violet hue, an agent economy can deter Sybil attacks by requiring each identity to anchor its public key to a time-locked collateral bond. Verifier contracts enforce periodic signed heartbeats and slash deposits for equivocation or missed epochs. Each fake identity thus locks scarce capital and risks slashing. However, wealthy attackers can still fund large Sybil pools, while steep bonds exclude honest newcomers.
